definition: Optimizing entire multi-step trajectories of an LLM agent (tool calls, environment feedback, intermediate decisions) rather than single responses.
details: Optimizing entire multi-step trajectories of an LLM agent (tool calls, environment feedback, intermediate decisions) rather than single responses. The hard parts are long-horizon credit assignment, expensive environment rollouts, and reward design for partially verifiable tasks; this is the training frontier behind current agentic models.

explainer.lead: Multi-turn RL optimizes entire multi-step trajectories of an LLM agent, including tool calls, environment feedback, and intermediate decisions, rather than single responses. It is the training frontier behind current agentic models.

tiers.eli5: Instead of grading one answer, you grade the whole conversation and every move the agent made along the way.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers optimize whole trajectories so agents learn from multi-step outcomes. The hard parts are long-horizon credit assignment, expensive environment rollouts, and reward design for partially verifiable tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: Optimization targets full multi-step trajectories rather than single responses; known difficulties are long-horizon credit assignment, costly rollouts, and reward design for partially verifiable tasks.

explainer.example: An agent makes several tool calls with environment feedback between them, and the whole sequence is scored and optimized rather than each response alone.
